compatibility_regressions: Changing recursive matching to a newly defined project-relative basis could alter previously unspecified behavior for patterns written against walked or target-relative paths.

Switching recursive discovery from self.config.ignore_paths to self._ignore_paths could prevent later configuration mutations from affecting discovery, despite no audited evidence that this behavior should change.
A broad project-relative-path implementation could diverge from the focused normalization fix demonstrated by hindsight evidence and affect more matching cases than necessary.
invented_requirements: Recursive ignore-path matching must use paths relative to the invocation/config project directory.
Recursive discovery must use the initialization-time captured ignore-path configuration rather than the live configuration value.
The regression test must prove exclusion by inspecting linted paths while also proving a non-ignored file remains linted.
The behavior must be covered end-to-end for both POSIX and Windows path forms.
The change must verify configuration precedence and all non-recursive semantics remain unchanged.
material_blockers: The contract seals project-relative matching semantics that are not established by the public request or audited repository evidence and are not demonstrated by the hindsight implementation.
The contract requires use of captured ignore-path configuration, but the repository audit explicitly identifies the intended source as unknown and hindsight evidence does not validate this change.

The acceptance checks do not match the observed regression shape: hindsight tests recursive discovery from the current directory and validates normalized path matching, rather than the sealed src/ project-configuration scenario and its broader path-basis guarantees.
redundant_questions: The config-source question forced a decision between captured and live values even though the reported failure and audited facts did not establish that configuration capture caused the bug.

The match-basis question offered project-relative semantics as the recommended solution before establishing whether simple normalization of the existing candidate path resolved the reported Windows/current-directory failure.
summary: The interview accurately retained every explicit owner answer, but it converted two repository unknowns into broad mandatory behavior without evidence that either was needed for the bug. Hindsight shows a narrower shared-path normalization fix and a current-directory regression test. Because the sealed contract would direct implementation toward unsupported path-basis and configuration-lifecycle changes, it is not implementation-ready despite complete owner recall.
